I need to clarify the onset of these symptoms: did your right leg weakness and unsteady gait start suddenly or gradually?

Also, have you noticed any specific memory lapses, such as forgetting recent conversations or getting lost in familiar places?

Finally, when did your paranoid behavior first begin, and does it seem related to your physical decline?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast and MRI Spine. Have you experienced any recent fevers, weight loss, or history of tuberculosis?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect. MRI Spine: Information not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neurosyphilis (Tabes Dorsalis with parenchymatous syphilis).
